questions.question_text:
Given below are four statements.
Statement 1: All students are inquisitive.
Statement 2: Some students are inquisitive.
Statement 3: No student is inquisitive.
Statement 4: Some students are not inquisitive.
From the given four statements, find the two statements that CANNOT BE
TRUE simultaneously, assuming that there is at least one student in the class.
questions.explaination: Statement 1 ("All students are inquisitive") and Statement 3 ("No student is inquisitive") are universal affirmative and universal negative statements (contraries). In classical categorical logic with a non-empty class, both statements cannot be simultaneously true.

questions.question_text:
Consider the relationships among P, Q, R, S, and T:
• P is the brother of Q.
• S is the daughter of Q.
• T is the sister of S.
• R is the mother of Q.
The following statements are made based on the relationships given above.
(1) R is the grandmother of S.
(2) P is the uncle of S and T.
(3) R has only one son.
(4) Q has only one daughter.
Which one of the following options is correct?

options.D:
Only (4) is true.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.explaination: Since R is the mother of Q and S is the daughter of Q, R is definitely the grandmother of S (statement 1 is true). P is the brother of Q, so P is the maternal/paternal uncle of Q's children S and T (statement 2 is true). The genders and number of other children of R and Q are not specified, so (3) and (4) cannot be established.

questions.question_text:
Based only on the conversation below, identify the logically correct inference:
“Even if I had known that you were in the hospital, I would not have gone there to
see you”, Ramya told Josephine.

options.A: Ramya knew that Josephine was in the hospital.
options.B: Ramya did not know that Josephine was in the hospital.
options.C: Ramya and Josephine were once close friends; but now, they are not.
options.D:
Josephine was in the hospital due to an injury to her leg.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.explaination: The subjunctive statement 'Even if I had known that you were in the hospital...' logically presupposes that the speaker did not know about Josephine's hospitalization at that time.

questions.question_text:
If IMAGE and FIELD are coded as FHBNJ and EMFJG respectively then, which
one among the given options is the most appropriate code for BEACH ?
questions.explaination: The coding rule applies a $+1$ alphabetical shift to each character followed by string reversal. Shifting $\text{BEACH}$ by $+1$ gives $\text{CFBDI}$, and reversing this yields $\text{IDBFC}$.
